**1 Blocker · 6 Should · 3 Questions · 2 Nits — 12 open.** The change does what the ticket asks and the shape is right: the scheduled path builds its own context and the branch is out of `ReportBuilder`. One blocker, and it is the composition of two reasonable-looking decisions rather than either of them.

**Method** · read the scheduled path, the column policy and the audit writer at `d41c8e2` · ran `php artisan test --filter=Export` · **2 suppressed** · **1 not verified** · **1 area not reviewed** — detail at the end

### Problem fit

A scheduled export used to build its context from a request that was never there, which is why the branch inside `ReportBuilder` existed at all. Giving the scheduled path a context of its own is the right shape for that. What is new is that the column policy now runs in two places, and the blocker below is where the two disagree.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Schedule due] --> B[Build its own context]
  B --> C{Columns named?}
  C -->|named| D[Narrow the select]
  C -->|none named| E[Every column exported]
```

### Open — needs a decision

| | Where | Finding | Status |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 🔴 Blocker · F9 | [`ColumnPolicy.php:52`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Reporting/ColumnPolicy.php#L52) | The column policy is skipped entirely when the definition names no columns | Open · on the code |
| 🟠 Should · F1 | [`ExportContext.php:47`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Reporting/ExportContext.php#L47) | An empty allowed-columns list means every column, not none | Open · on the code |
| 🟠 Should · F3 | [`DispatchScheduledExports.php:61`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Console/Commands/DispatchScheduledExports.php#L61) | A schedule whose tenant row has gone is dispatched anyway | Open · on the code |
| 🟠 Should · F6 | [`ColumnPolicy.php:31`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Reporting/ColumnPolicy.php#L31) | The policy is applied after the query is built, so a hidden column is still selected | Open · on the code |
| 🟠 Should · F11 | [`ExportController.php:41`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Http/Controllers/ExportController.php#L41) | The web path builds its context from the request with no tenant check | Open · on the code |
| 🟠 Should · F13 | [`RunScheduledExport.php:116`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Jobs/RunScheduledExport.php#L116) | A soft-deleted tenant is exported; only a hard-deleted one is skipped | Open · on the code |
| 🟠 Should · F14 | [the pull request](https://github.com/acme/portal/pull/514) | The description does not say what happens to an export that is skipped | Open · in the body |
| 🔵 Question · F5 | [`ExportPipeline.php:71`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Reporting/ExportPipeline.php#L71) | Two schedules for one tenant at once would write the audit entry twice | Open · on the code |
| 🔵 Question · F7 | [`RunScheduledExport.php:94`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Jobs/RunScheduledExport.php#L94) | Nothing says what happens to a schedule whose definition was deleted | Open · on the code |
| 🔵 Question · F12 | [`RecordsAnExport.php:22`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Audit/RecordsAnExport.php#L22) | Whether the audit entry still fits is not established | Open · in the body |
| ⚪ Nit · F4 | [`ScheduleToContext.php:18`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Reporting/ScheduleToContext.php#L18) | The class is named for the direction, not for what it makes | Open · in the body |
| ⚪ Nit · F10 | [`ReportBuilder.php:28`](https://github.com/acme/portal/blob/d41c8e2/app/Reporting/ReportBuilder.php#L28) | The removed branch leaves a comment describing it | Open · on the code |

### Should · F14 · The description does not say what happens to an export that is skipped

Three of the change's early returns each decide what an export produces, and none of them appears in the description. Three sentences under “What is skipped” would answer the question a reader otherwise has to read the job for.

### Question · F12 · Whether the audit entry still fits is not established

`RecordsAnExport` is outside this change, and the scheduled path passes it a system actor with no id. Is `export_audit.actor_id` nullable, and does its consumer read a null actor as a system export?

### Nit · F4 · The class is named for the direction, not for what it makes

The two siblings in this namespace are named for what they return. This one is named for the direction of the conversion, so it does not read with them.

<details><summary>How this review was made — scope, suppressed findings, what I could not verify</summary>

Read the scheduled path, the column policy, the audit writer and the two controllers at `d41c8e2`; ran the export suite.

**Suppressed (2)** · a redaction helper's naming, because the file is replaced by ABC-418 next week · a Horizon queue name, which this change does not reach.

**Not verified (1)** · that the nightly dispatch really does run two schedules for one tenant in the same minute; the question is F5 and the answer is the author's.

**Not reviewed (1)** · the reporting front end, which reads the same definitions but was not changed.

</details>

sections.heading: ### Blocker · F9 · The column policy is skipped entirely when the definition names no columns
sections.title: The column policy is skipped entirely when the definition names no columns
sections.text: Two decisions compose here. The array cast answers `[]` for a null column, and this early return reads `[]` as “no policy” — so a definition older than the migration exports every column, including the two its tenant's policy hides. Eleven definitions in staging are in that state with an active schedule.

sections.heading: ### Should · F1 · An empty allowed-columns list means every column, not none
sections.title: An empty allowed-columns list means every column, not none
sections.text: `allowed_columns` arrives here as `[]` for any definition whose column was never written, and every reader downstream treats an empty list as “nothing to narrow”. `ColumnPolicy::for()` already draws the distinction the web path needs; this path could call it.

sections.heading: ### Should · F3 · A schedule whose tenant row has gone is dispatched anyway
sections.title: A schedule whose tenant row has gone is dispatched anyway
sections.text: A schedule whose tenant row is gone is dispatched and then fails inside `ExportContext::forSchedule` with a null dereference, four frames deep. Filtering the dispatch query on the tenant's existence makes the same failure readable.
sections.agent_title: A schedule whose tenant row has gone is dispatched anyway
sections.agent_text: A schedule whose tenant row is gone is dispatched and then fails inside `ExportContext::forSchedule` with a null dereference, four frames deep. Filtering the dispatch query on the tenant's existence makes the same failure readable.

sections.heading: ### Should · F6 · The policy is applied after the query is built, so a hidden column is still selected
sections.title: The policy is applied after the query is built, so a hidden column is still selected
sections.text: The policy narrows rows that are already in memory, so the hidden columns are selected and read before they are dropped. `ReportBuilder::withPolicy()` narrows the `select` instead.

sections.title: The web path builds its context from the request with no tenant check
sections.text: The removed branch called `ReportPolicy::view()` before building the context, and the call went with it. `download()` still authorises; `stream()`, reachable from the signed-URL route added in #496, does not.

sections.heading: ### Should · F13 · A soft-deleted tenant is exported; only a hard-deleted one is skipped
sections.title: A soft-deleted tenant is exported; only a hard-deleted one is skipped
sections.text: The guard skips the job and not the schedule: `next_run_at` is advanced before the job runs, so a trashed tenant's schedule is dispatched and skipped every night. Schedule 118 has done that 39 times since September with no audit row to show for it.

sections.title: Two schedules for one tenant at once would write the audit entry twice
sections.text: Can two schedules for one tenant be due in the same minute? Both would write an audit row keyed on the tenant and the date, and the unique index on that pair was dropped in #502.

held_back.claim: The superseded accessor `TenantContext::tenantForRequest()` is still public with nothing marking it superseded, so the next person who needs a tenant reads the accessor that is still there, reaches for the obvious name, and writes a second call path into the export code this change exists to remove — and because the `@deprecated` annotation is what the static analyser reads, that second caller is found in review by somebody rather than failing the build on the way in.
